[https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/92d6a0500b9f528a9adcd6bbcda46ebf9b6baf03/src/_pytest/python.py#L274-L292](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/92d6a0500b9f528a9adcd6bbcda46ebf9b6baf03/src/_pytest/python.py#L274-L292)

This line of code `return s.replace(".[", "[")` causes the problem. We should replace it with `return s`. After changing this, run `tox -e linting,py37`, pass all the tests and resolve this issue. But I can't find this line of code for what purpose.

The issue is that `s.replace(".[", "[")` replaces ALL occurrences of `.[` in the string, including those that are part of parameter values. The intent of this replacement is to handle cases where a parameterized test node's name contains `[`, and the `.join` creates something like `test_module.TestClass.test_func.[param]` - the `.[` should become `[` to get `test_module.TestClass.test_func[param]`.

But the problem is that if a parameter value itself contains `.[`, it gets incorrectly modified.

The fix should be more targeted - only replace the `.[` that appears between the test function name and the parameter bracket, not within parameter values.


Looking at how the parts are constructed, each node's name gets added to the list. For a parameterized test like `test_boo[.[]`, that bracket notation is part of the node name itself, so when joined with dots it becomes something like `module.test_boo[.[]`. The issue is that the parameter value itself might contain `.[`, which shouldn't be modified.

The fix is to only replace `.[` that occurs at the boundary between the function name and the parameter brackets. Since the `[` that starts the parameter section is always the first `[` in the last part, we should only replace `.[` that appears right before the first `[` (i.e., the one that separates the test name from its parameters).
